newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress panel delays re-election vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress panel delays re-election vote.

text.p: A special committee of the Brazilian lower house Tuesday agreed to delay until Wednesday a vote on a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to seek re-election, officials said.
Panel officials said deputies voted 29 to one to put off a vote on the bill until Wednesday at 1000 local time/0700 EST/1200 GMT.

Officials said the postponement of the vote, engineered by government allies, was intended to give deputies from Brazil's largest political party, the Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), time to sort out their stance.
A PMDB convention on Sunday stunned the government by recommending party members vote against re-election.
PMDB delegates also recommended the party try to put off a ballot on re-election until elections for the presidencies of the lower and upper houses had been completed in early February.
"We need 24 hours to reach a clear position on this," PMDB panel member Deputy Carlos Henrique Alves told Bandeirante television in a live report from the committee chamber.
Fearing the establishment of oligarchies, Brazil has not allowed the re-election of sitting presidents since the republic was created in 1889.
